chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara and Bukayr and Al-Fudayl and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Buraed al-Ijli, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that the two said:

Regarding the man who is among one of these sects/followers of personal desires – the Haruriyya, and the Murji'ah, and the Uthmaniyya, and the Qadariyya – then he repents and recognizes this matter (Wilayah) and improves his view: Does he have to repeat every Salat he prayed, or Sawm, or Zakat, or Hajj, or is there no repeating upon him of anything from that?

He (peace be upon him) said: There is no repeating upon him of anything from that, other than the Zakat. It is inevitable that he pays it, because he placed the Zakat in a place other than its proper place, and rather, its proper place is the people of Wilayah.
ai.seo_question: Do acts of worship need to be repeated if a person repents from a theological sect?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that while theological deviations in sects like the Haruriyya or Qadariyya do not invalidate the fundamental pillars of worship (salah, sawm, hajj) upon repentance, they do affect the validity of Zakat. The ruling emphasizes the Shia principle that Zakat is specifically designated for the 'Ahl al-Wilayah' (the Imams and their deputies), meaning payment to others is considered misplaced and requires re-payment, highlighting the political-theological link between spiritual authority and fiscal obligation.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Zurara, and Bukeyr, and Al Fuzayl, and Muhammad Bin Muslim, and Bureyd Al Ijaly, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>,

both having said regarding the man who happens to be among one of these followers of personal desires – the Harouriyya, and the Murjiyya, and the Usmaniyya, and the Qadariyya. Then he repents and recognises this matter (Al-Wilayah), and his view (Emān) improves. Would he have to repeat every Salāt he had prayed, or Soām (Fast), or Zakāt, or Hajj, or there isn’t anything upon him to repeat from that?’

Heasws said: ‘There is no repeating upon him from that other than the Zakāt. It is inevitable that he pays it, because he had placed the Zakāt in other that is (appropriate) place, and rather, its (appropriate) place is the people of Al-Wilayah’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn ’Udhaynah from Zurarah, Bukayr, al-Fudayl, Muhammad ibn Muslim and Burayd al-‘Ijliy who have said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, and abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhim al-Salam,

were asked about the case of one who follows such opinions as al-Harawriyah, al-Murji’ah, al-‘Uthmaniyah and al-Qadriyah. He then repents and recognizes this issue (the Divine Authority of ’A’immah) and corrects his opinion, is he required to perform the Qada’ (compensatory prayer for) all of his Salah (prayer), fasting, payment of Zakat and Hajj; or is he not required to do them again?

He (the Imam) said, ‘He is not required to do any of these things again, except Zakat which is necessary to be paid because he has placed it improperly. The proper place for it is people of al-Wilayah (people who acknowledge Divine Authority of ’A’immah, ‘Alayhim al-Sa^m).’”
